channel.description: Latest articles from The Copper Courier (coppercourier.com)

item.title: As Arizona braces for Medicaid reforms, many patients don’t know how to qualify for hospital debt forgiveness
item.description: As some Arizonans brace for the effects of Medicaid changes, more patients across the state may need to rely on hospital financial assistance.

item.title: Sky Harbor appeals to the public to donate to unpaid TSA workers
item.description: Amid a partial government shutdown affecting workers at Phoenix Sky Harbor, the airport is asking Arizona residents to support employees who continue to show up despite not being paid.

item.title: WATCH: Southern Arizona could house a new ICE detention center
item.description: Marana could see a new 500-bed ICE detention center. Here’s the deal.

item.title: WATCH: Kyrene educator calls on GOP lawmakers to better fund public schools
item.description: Delia Lyding, a math interventionist in Kyrene Elementary School District, wants the state Legislature's majority party to show their support for educators with actions, not just words.

item.title: Why are grasshoppers everywhere in Phoenix right now? Here's the cause
item.description: Grasshoppers are a common sight across Arizona, but why does it seem like there’s an excess of them right now?

item.title: Chandler eighth grader wins Arizona Spelling Bee, heads to nationals
item.description: Esha Marupudi, a 14-year-old eighth grader at BASIS Chandler, won the Arizona Spelling Bee, successfully defending her title by correctly spelling “penicillate” in the final round.

item.title: No Kings protests set to return. See every rally in metro Phoenix
item.description: Opponents of President Donald Trump are planning to participate in thousands of No Kings protests in Arizona and across the nation on March 28.

item.title: 'One less good guy': Readers react to César Chávez sexual assault allegations
item.description: The recent allegations of sexual abuse against César Chávez have sent a shockwave through communities. Here's how our readers reacted.

item.title: WATCH: Arizona teacher says low pay is driving educators out of the profession
item.description: As teacher pay fails to rise, Arizona educators are pushed to choose between raising a family and being there for their community, said Emmett Burnton, Deer Valley Unified School District history teacher.

item.title: End of an era: Who will care for Arivaca when its only doctor retires?
item.description: Dr. Donald Smith, 67, has been trying to retire for just over a year. However, the search for his replacement at his Arivaca clinic has been far from easy.
